title: Post-Bite-30 Backlog Reconciliation Against Production Baseline

scope.description: All GitHub issues that were open when issue #853 was created, excluding #853 itself because it is the reconciliation driver rather than backlog being classified.

items.title: next steps
items.rationale: The original architecture-to-code checklist is fully represented in the Production tree: GORM-backed database access, SQL migrations, Fiber HTTP routes, and a React router/page application all exist.

items.title: React page/route skeleton
items.rationale: The frontend has a production route graph covering People, Collaborators, Expenses, Work Periods, receipts, and administration pages.

items.title: Service Layer Validation Roles To be enforced
items.rationale: Several bundled rules are enforced (for example one open Collaborator Journey per Membership and pending commission accrual when production is missing), but other original rules such as the 30-day return wait and max-sick-day enforcement are still only configuration/documented intent rather than complete executable policy.

evidence.contains: Membership already has an open Collaborator Journey
Gold production is missing for this work period and location

items.title: implement the environment files logic
items.rationale: Repository-owned environment initialization/rendering and per-environment server configuration are implemented and used by deployment tooling.

items.title: Add E2E tests for Person
items.rationale: People E2E coverage exists for create, filter/pagination, view switching, required-field validation, duplicate CPF, and cellular validation.

evidence.contains: Tenant Administrator can create a Person and define the initial temporary password

items.title: Add a filter to Person list
items.rationale: The People landing page has live search plus status/profile/collaborator-eligibility filters and card/list views.

evidence.contains: user can filter and paginate the People page

items.title: Implement person tests for front end
items.rationale: Frontend unit coverage exists for People list/detail/form behavior in addition to E2E coverage.

items.title: Add Authentication and Authorization
items.rationale: The original JWT/header-era proposal is no longer the architecture. Production uses login-backed sessions plus canonical Authentication Account -> AccountActor -> exact Actor/Tenant authorization; Bite 30D explicitly separates intrinsic self-service authority from delegated Role Grants, and later Bite 30 slices harden session, Tenant-selection, and isolation boundaries.

evidence.contains: Roles and Role Grants now represent delegated authority only

items.title: Refactor to a cloud first architecture
items.rationale: The issue specifies a Google Cloud/Terraform target, while the actual Production baseline is Docker Compose on a Hetzner-hosted server behind Caddy and SQLite. Relevant contract/database follow-ups survive as separate backlog issues; the original umbrella direction is no longer the deployed architecture.

items.title: Wiring this spec into your Go/React projects
items.rationale: OpenAPI contracts and generated Go/TypeScript artifacts exist, but the original api/spec/full.yaml-as-single-contract/runtime-generated-client wiring is not the current implementation and generated types are not the sole runtime boundary.

items.title: Abstract the DB driver config
items.rationale: Production database opening is SQLite-specific; there is no runtime DB_DRIVER switch or PostgreSQL GORM driver abstraction.

items.title: Implement and validate the People update flow
items.rationale: People update is implemented with backend validation/uniqueness handling and frontend detail/edit tests.

items.title: Design and implement a safe bulk-import
items.rationale: A People CSV importer, CLI command, dry-run Make target, validation tests, and all-or-nothing import behavior are present.

items.title: Marinaldo Brito missing RG
items.rationale: The named Person record is not present as an actionable Production record, so there is no RG correction to perform. The issue was closed after the owner confirmed that the record had been removed/not added; it no longer represents an outstanding Production-data defect.

githubDecision.decision: The named Person record is not present, so there is no record to correct.

items.title: A few person use cases
items.rationale: The People UI supports search/filtering, Active/Inactive-style status filters, card/list presentation, and navigation from a displayed Person to the full Person record.

items.title: There is no reference data for Periodo
items.rationale: The canonical reference-data seed has no Diurno/Noturno (day/night period) reference type; Work Period naming remains shift-like rather than backed by the requested reference data.

items.title: I, as an application user, when adding avperson's recoerd, if the nicknameis blank, I want the app to use the person's first name
items.rationale: Production intentionally continues to require an explicit Person nickname on create and update. After reviewing the implemented behavior, the product decision is to preserve that model and learn from operational use before reconsidering Person naming semantics; automatic nickname = firstName defaulting is therefore not planned.

githubDecision.decision: Preserve required explicit nickname behavior and learn from Production practice before changing Person naming semantics.

items.title: Should we allow Editing expenese
items.rationale: The product has made the safer decision: incorrect Expenses are not edited in place in the UI; they are cancelled with an auditable reversal and recreated as a replacement. The original open-ended design question is therefore obsolete.

evidence.contains: Incorrect Expenses are not edited in place.

items.title: Use nickname in the Work Plan Inform Form
items.rationale: The Inform workflow now exposes collaborator nickname, including absence warnings and printed roster rows, but printed roster rows still render full name first and nickname second rather than using nickname as the primary displayed identity.

items.title: Write an e2e test to validate pending receipts
items.rationale: The requested exact lifecycle is covered: create debit receipt, confirm outstanding, open printable receipt, return with signed reference, and confirm it disappears from outstanding receipts.

evidence.contains: outstanding receipt appears, can be opened, and disappears after signed return

items.title: Implement I18N infrastructure
items.rationale: The frontend has no i18next/react-i18next dependency or localization bootstrap. The parent i18n initiative remains open.

items.title: Integrate real authentication
items.rationale: Production has first-party login-backed authentication accounts, hashed session tokens, HTTP-only session cookies, password change/reset, session revocation, account deactivation/reactivation, and E2E login coverage.

evidence.contains: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_sessions
authenticated user can see identity, tenant, sign out, and sign back in

items.title: Bite-621 i18n Implementation - common
items.rationale: No common localization framework is present in the Production frontend.

items.title: Bite: i18n Implementation - people
items.rationale: People UI strings remain hard-coded English and there is no localization runtime to supply translated People resources.

items.title: Bite: i18n Implementation - planning
items.rationale: Planning UI strings remain hard-coded English and there is no localization runtime.

items.title: Bite: i18n Implementation - expenses
items.rationale: Expense UI strings remain hard-coded English and there is no localization runtime.

evidence.contains: Incorrect Expenses are not edited in place.

items.title: Bite: i18n Implementation - receipts
items.rationale: Receipt UI strings remain hard-coded English and there is no localization runtime.

items.title: [Use Case]: Backend database should be changed to postgresql from sqllite, for better peformance.
items.rationale: The Production database implementation is still SQLite and no PostgreSQL driver is present.

items.title: [Use Case]: Production database backup should be backed up periodically - daily/weekly
items.rationale: Production deployments take and verify a pre-migration SQLite backup, and backup targets/scripts exist, but the repository does not install or enforce a periodic daily/weekly Production backup schedule.

items.title: [Use Case]: IP Address of logged in user has to be stored in db table. multi device tracking.
items.rationale: Authentication sessions already persist IP address and User-Agent, but there is no durable device identity, device authorization workflow, or access restriction to authorized devices.

items.title: [Use Case]: Need to define our application users, and to quantify for our SAAS license purpose.
items.rationale: Bite 30 establishes a canonical Authentication Account/AccountActor identity and sessions can represent multiple devices, providing a sound user-counting foundation. There is still no SaaS license metric, concurrent-device policy, shared-credential prevention control, or usage-report implementation.

evidence.contains: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_sessions

items.title: [Use Case]: Our product supports multi-tenancy- we need to introduce SAAS license management module
items.rationale: There is no SaaS license, renewal, subscription, or tenant usage-report module in the Production application.

items.title: [Use Case]: ERS - Multi tenancy
items.rationale: Bite 30 replaced the issue's early tenant_id/policy concept with the canonical AccountActor/Membership model and comprehensive cross-Tenant authorization, identity, operational-domain, and financial-isolation coverage.

evidence.contains: same Global Person keeps self-service financial records isolated by selected Tenant without browser cache leakage

notes: Issues #63 and #130 remain in scope because they were open when issue #853 was created, but later owner decisions closed them and make their requested changes non-actionable.
Completed Bite 30D issue #708 is baseline architecture evidence for the supersession of the earlier generic authentication/authorization issue #20.
